x.description:
The x coordinates of the bars. See also align for the alignment of the bars to the coordinates.

Python: sequence of scalars

height.description:
The height(s) of the bars.

Python: scalar or sequence of scalars

width.description:
The width(s) of the bars (default: 0.8).

Python: scalar or array-like

bottom.description:
The y coordinate(s) of the bars bases (default: 0).

Python: scalar or array-like

color.description:
The colors of the bar faces.

Python: scalar or array-like

edgeColor.description:
The colors of the bar edges.
(matplotlib edgecolor)

Python: scalar or array-like

lineWidth.description:
Width of the bar edge(s). If 0, don't draw edges.
(matplotlib linewidth)

Python: scalar or array-like

tickLabel.description:
The tick labels of the bars. Default: None (Use default numeric labels.)
(matplotlib tick_label)

Python: string or array-like

xErr.description:
If not None, add horizontal / vertical errorbars to the bar tips. The values are +/- sizes relative to the data:
(matplotlib xerr)

Python: scalar or array-like of shape(N,) or shape(2,N)

yErr.description:
If not None, add horizontal / vertical errorbars to the bar tips. The values are +/- sizes relative to the data:
(matplotlib yerr)

Python: scalar or array-like of shape(N,) or shape(2,N)

eColor.description:
The line color of the errorbars.
(matplotlib ecolor)

Python: scalar or array-like

capSize.description:
The length of the error bar caps in points. Default: None, which will take the value from rcParams["errorbar.capsize"].
(matplotlib capsize)

Python: scalar

errorKw.description:
Dictionary of kwargs to be passed to the errorbar method. Values of ecolor or capsize defined here take precedence over the independent kwargs.
(matplotlib error_kw)

log.description: If True, set the y-axis to be log scale.

orientation.description:
This is for internal use only. Please use barh for horizontal bar plots. Default: 'vertical'.

Python: {'vertical', 'horizontal'}

align.description:
Alignment of the bars to the x coordinates:

Python: {'center', 'edge'}
